html:
The Jawoyn are an Aboriginal Australian people of the Katherine region of the Northern Territory, on the southern edge of Arnhem Land. The map shows them from 1600 to 1815.

Their country holds the gorges of the Katherine River and many rock art sites, some showing very long human use. Their neighbours included the Mangarayi and Ngalakgan to the southeast and the Warray to the northwest.

The Overland Telegraph Line crossed their land in the early 1870s, and gold found near Pine Creek while it was being built set off a rush of European and Chinese miners. Cattle stations followed. In 1989 the Katherine Gorge national park was handed back to the Jawoyn under land rights law and renamed Nitmiluk; they lease it back to the government as a park.
sum: The Jawoyn are an Aboriginal Australian people of the Katherine region of the Northern Territory, on the southern edge of Arnhem Land. The map shows them from 1600 to 1815.
